verdict.rationale: Dagster ships its own CLI tooling (dg, create-dagster) and programmatic APIs for launching runs. It also has a daemon-driven deployment that runs schedules, sensors and declarative automation without user interaction, so non-interactive automation is a first-party capability. However, the cited CLI usage is scaffolding and `dg dev` (which starts a webserver), and nothing documents launching runs from a CI pipeline. Missing for 10: documented headless run/launch CLI commands, explicit CI integration guidance (e.g., running jobs or asset checks in GitHub Actions), exit-code/non-interactive behavior docs, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: You can scaffold Dagster Component definitions in your project from the command line with the `dg scaffold defs` command
Use Dagster's UI or APIs to run subsets of your dbt models, seeds, and snapshots.
A typical Dagster Docker deployment includes a several long-running containers: one for the webserver, one for the daemon, and one for each code location.
Schedules enable automated execution of jobs at specified intervals.
